_about: Staged silhouettes: for every background / character / position the scenario uses, the background photo is edited by the Codex CLI's image generation to hold that person in a fitting pose, painted flat magenta; tools/yonaki/pictures.py cuts the magenta out as the mask. Keys are bg/character/position. 'who' overrides the character's description, 'where' the position's region.
_common: Edit the attached photograph. Keep every part of the photo exactly as it is: the same framing, perspective, lighting, colours and objects; do not redraw, crop, shift or restyle anything. Add exactly one person: {who}, {pose}. Place the person {where}. The person is a main character seen up close: put them in the near foreground or the near middle ground, so that a standing person is at least half the image height (a sitting person or one partly hidden by furniture proportionally), in correct perspective with the floor and furniture. Do not make the person small or far away unless the pose below says so. Anything in front of the person (furniture, seat backs, counters, tub rims, water, railings) must stay in front and hide those parts of the person. Paint the person ONLY as one completely flat, uniform, pure magenta (#FF00FF) silhouette: no shading, texture, outline, glow or soft edge, no shadow or reflection, and no other magenta anywhere in the image. Keep the same image size.

_where.l: in the left part of the image, the whole person between 5% and 40% of the image width from the left edge
_where.c: near the horizontal centre of the image, the whole person between 32% and 68% of the image width
_where.r: in the right part of the image, the whole person between 60% and 95% of the image width from the left edge
